newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN MILITARY PRAISES LAW-ABIDING MEGAWATI.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN MILITARY PRAISES LAW-ABIDING MEGAWATI.

text.p: Indonesia's powerful military has praised ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri for obeying the law, the Jakarta Post newspaper said on Wednesday.

Armed forces head of socio-political affairs Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid said there was no evidence Megawati, who has been questioned four times by police since her government-backed ouster but never charged, had broken any laws.

Megawati was removed from her position as chairman of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) at a congress, backed and funded by the government and military, in June last year and is still challenging the action in the courts.
She was replaced by deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi.
"Megawati has always been constitutional in her actions," Hamid told reporters. "She always rejects illegal and unconstitutional ways of settling problems."
The military has a powerful role in Indonesia's tightly controlled political system through its socio-political branch and intelligence agencies.

Recent reports suggest Megawati and her supporters in the PDI are considering launching a new challenge for the party leadership at its next congress in 1998 and have rejected any talk of reconciliation with the faction of her rival Surjadi.
Megawati has not made public her position on running for the party leadership. She has maintained that Surjadi's takeover was illegal.
Hamid said he doubted a party congress could settle the PDI's problems.
"Can they guarantee that the congress will settle the problems? The two factions can't even agree on a date for the congress," he said.
Surjadi failed to gain enough votes to win a seat in the current parliament when he ran at the top of the party's ticket in the capital Jakarta.
